summary:
[trial 1]: With BTC at $95,000 on 2026-04-26, the target of closing above $100,000 requires only a ~5.3% gain (ln(100/95) ≈ 0.051) over roughly 8 months of remaining runway. At BTC's historical annualized volatility of ~65%, the one-sigma move over 8 months is ~±49%, making a 5.3% hurdle well under one-tenth of a standard deviation — statistically trivial for this asset. The primary bearish risk is cycle timing: the April 2024 halving puts the historical cycle peak window at roughly Q4 2025–Q1 2026, meaning BTC at $95K in late April 2026 could reflect a post-peak correction rather than consolidation before further upside. If the cycle high was, say, $130K–$150K in late 2025 and BTC has been declining, downward momentum could keep it below $100K through year-end. However, even under a mildly bearish cycle interpretation, the sheer proximity of the target and the length of the remaining window give bulls multiple re-entry opportunities. Base-rate reasoning on 'will a volatile asset with ~65% annualized vol cross a level 5% above its current price over 8 months' strongly favors yes. Probability set at 0.74, reflecting high base-rate probability discounted modestly for post-halving cycle headwinds and macro uncertainty.

[trial 2]: As of 2026-04-26, BTC sits at $95,000 — just 5.26% below the $100,000 threshold, with roughly 8 months remaining until the Dec 31 deadline. A simple lognormal model (annualized vol ~65%, drift near zero) places the year-end close above $100K at approximately 50%, but several factors push the estimate higher: the small absolute gap, the 8-month runway (multiple vol windows), continued institutional ETF inflows, and the psychological magnetism of the round number. Countervailing forces include post-halving cycle fatigue (the April 2024 halving is now ~24 months old, historically a window where BTC bull momentum fades), the possibility that $95K represents a retracement from a prior ATH, and macro uncertainty around rates and risk appetite in 2026. On net, the proximity of the target and time remaining dominate — the price needs only one sustained leg up — but cycle timing introduces meaningful downside risk, keeping the estimate comfortably above coin-flip but well short of certainty.
